purpose: One real ROS/RViz synchronous replay of an autonomously searched FR06 tight-corridor plan.

map.runtime_copy_note: run_demo.sh with --scale 1.0 still copies the map through tools/scale_map_runtime.py into a mktemp directory and removes it on exit, so the runtime copy no longer exists. Re-running the same tool with the same source directory and scale 1.0 reproduces map.pgm b59dc888... and scene_meta.yaml c1e85f2a..., and rewrites map.yaml to 7904204c6113579d088f442c25d8dbb7d9067fccb37aeefd861913fbf23c110d (same origin/resolution).

goal_path.note: The launch file prints its default bridge parameters before the scene_meta override; the admitted request logged at line 88 is start=(6.000, 6.000, 0.000) goal=(10.000, 10.000, 1.571).

plan.admission: admitted from cargo_wedge: start=(6.000, 6.000, 0.000) goal=(10.000, 10.000, 1.571) free_headings=True reverse=True

playback.rate_observation: The /formation_playback/rate parameter was set to 100 by the launch request, but the observed PLAYING-to-HOLD_END wall duration was 33.045 s, i.e. the replay ran at approximately 1x. No acceleration is claimed.

screenshots.overlay_caution: The RViz overlay text is the inherited FR05 display caution. It says that the playback layer itself reports no independent metric; it is not a failure of this plan. Quantitative evidence for FR06 comes from the FR02 audit JSON, not from this overlay.

scope_notes: This replay used the live planner node. Its plan carries plan_id 600000 and the launch-derived formation name cargo_wedge, so its model digest differs from the offline FR06 plans (6201-6203, formation_id fr06_three_vehicle) even though both end at T_end=33.02449442722614 s.
No hash-equality claim is made between the live plan and the offline plans; equality of T_end and of the logged geometry is what is observed.
This is one visual synchronous replay of one tight-corridor success. It is not a success-rate measurement.
